title: How to build an approval matrix for a real estate finance team
summary: An approval matrix for a property group should include thresholds that vary by spend type, amount, authority that runs per entity, and a clear backup for an approver. This guide explains how to design one, and how to adapt it to your business.
body_markdown:
In most established real estate firms, the finance teams usually know who to reach out to to approve an invoice or payment. In many cases, this is just common knowledge among the teams and isn't formally documented.


That said, this process, as streamlined as it may be, can face problems if, say, a new manager takes over the finance team or an auditor asks where those approval limits are formally documented.


This is where having an approval matrix is essential and is considered a best practice for[spend management for any real estate group](https://www.alaan.com/industries/real-estate) . This guide will walk you through how to design one and highlight the common mistakes that cause it to fail, and more.


## What is an approval matrix?


An approval matrix, also referred to as the delegation of authority approval matrix, is a document that states who can commit the business to spending, up to what amount, and under what conditions.


In the UAE, the directors' statutory authority is governed by UAE company law and each company's constitutional documents. However, most day-to-day financial approval limits are established through internal governance rather than legislation, and that is where an approval matrix is required.


## What are the key parameters that a well-designed approval matrix should cover?


The correct way to design an approval matrix for a real estate firm is to design it around the key operational decisions it has to make on a daily basis, such as:


### Set thresholds by amount


The approval matrix should create thresholds that reduce unnecessary escalation without removing meaningful financial oversight. In simple terms, there should be a clear definition of who can approve spend up to AED 5,000 for, say, simple day-to-day expenses, or beyond AED 500,000 for property acquisitions.


Keep in mind there are just illustrative numbers. The actual figures should reflect the size and complexity of your business.


### Differentiate by spend type


The approval matrix should set separate threshold columns for operating expenditure, capital expenditure, and contractual commitments. Take, for example, an AED 50,000 supplier invoice and an AED 50,000 capital commitment. The amount may be the same, but the latter should ideally require a higher level of approval authority.


Doing so will ensure that approval authority reflects the risk rather than transaction value alone.


### Define authority per entity


Every SPV in a property generally has its own board, its own accounts, and often its own external stakeholders. The approval matrix should reflect this and build approval authority around each legal entity.


### Plan for an approver's absence


Every approval matrix should clearly identify who can act when the primary approver is unavailable, under what circumstances temporary authority applies, and whether retrospective review is required once the primary approver returns. As best practice, every approval level should include at least one documented alternate approver.


Here is how all of what has been discussed above should translate into practice.


Type of Spend Site or Property Manager Finance manager CFO Board


Operating expenses Up to AED 10,000 Up to AED 50,000 Up to AED 250,000 Above AED 250,000


Capital expenditure No authority Up to AED 25,000 Up to AED 150,000 Above AED 150,000


Supplier contracts (new or renewal) No authority Up to AED 100,000 total contract value Up to AED 500,000 Above AED 500,000


Subcontractor payments Up to AED 15,000 per instruction Up to AED 75,000 Up to AED 300,000 Above AED 300,000


Property acquisitions No authority No authority Recommends to board All acquisitions


Please note that these figures are illustrative, and approval limits should always be determined by your organisation's governance framework, board resolutions and Articles of Association.


If you pay close attention, you will also realise that capital expenditure has a lower ceiling at every level than operating expenses, as the former creates a long-term financial commitment for the business. Supplier contracts also receive greater executive oversight for the same reason.


Before you finalise your approval matrix, you should know that under[Article 23 of the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 32 of 2021 on Commercial Companies](https://uaelegislation.gov.ae/en/legislations/1542/download) , a manager has full authority to bind the company in the ordinary course of management. This unless the company's MOA, AOA, or the manager's appointment contract explicitly restricts that authority.


## The other most important aspect of approval matrix design: Segregation of duties


While the approval matrix defines who can authorise how much of which spending, there also needs to be a check on how much control a person has over the process. This is what segregation of duties determines.


It is one of the first areas an auditor will review because it reduces the risk of errors, conflicts of interest and fraud. It's also identified as a core element of effective internal financial control by the[COSO Internal Control Framework](https://www.coso.org/guidance-on-ic) .


Segregation of duties should focus on addressing the following scenario combinations:


- **Requesting and approving** : The person requesting expenditure should not normally approve it themselves.
- **Approving and paying** : Authorising an invoice and releasing the payment should remain separate responsibilities.
- **Setting up suppliers and paying them** : The person setting up new suppliers should also not be the person in charge of paying them.


Now, applying these practices can be impractical in smaller teams; you must work around it by building in a compensating control in the form of, for example:


- Secondary review by the CFO
- Periodic board oversight
- Exception reporting
- Independent bank reconciliation


Such gaps often come to light during an[audit of purchases,](https://www.alaan.com/blog/audit-of-purchases) so it's worth treating those findings as input to refine your existing matrix design.


## How to implement an approval matrix effectively?


At the end of the day, an approval matrix is simply a document, albeit an important one. It's only effective when it's being actively followed and cannot account for manual errors, such as a finance manager approving a capital expenditure item miscoded as an operating expense.


The most effective way to implement an approval matrix is to bake it into your financial systems by[automating expense approvals](https://www.alaan.com/blog/automate-expense-management-approvals) . What this does is, rather than checking if everything happened as it should after the fact, the approval rules are enforced at the time of the spend.

## Summing it up


An approval matrix is effective only when employees can apply it consistently, and auditors can follow every reason behind every approval decision. As a property group, that means moving beyond simple value thresholds and integrating it into your existing financial infrastructure.


An approval matrix becomes much more effective when approval rules are enforced automatically instead of relying on manual checks.

## FAQ


**What is an approval matrix?**


An approval matrix is a document that defines who can approve different types of expenditure in an organisation based on factors such as transaction value, spend category, legal entity or business function.


**What is an authorisation matrix?**


An authorisation matrix is the same thing as an approval matrix or delegation of authority matrix. The terms are often used interchangeably.


**How do you design an approval matrix?**


Start by identifying approval thresholds, categorising different types of expenditure, assigning authority by legal entity or business function, documenting alternate approvers and separating incompatible responsibilities. The matrix should then be reviewed and approved as part of the organisation's governance framework.


**How many approval levels should an organisation have?**


There is no fixed number for how many approval levels an organisation must have. The number should balance financial control with operational efficiency.
